turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that?
Ms. Kalinowski, the zero went in without a call to you. That was wrong and I'm sorry. I'd like to take the meeting in the order you want.
Okay. Then the first thing I want is the zero withdrawn. Today. Put it in writing, Mr. Hale, or tell me why you can't.
Thank you. I should tell you I value the way Owen participates in class. He asks sharp questions about Ophelia. Do you read with him at home?
Owen's grades are not the subject of this meeting. Are you withdrawing the zero or not?
Sorry, hold on. Principal Reyes just walked in. Principal, this is Ms. Kalinowski. Ms. Kalinowski, do you mind if the principal sits in? Principal, what do you make of all this?
Fine. She can sit. But I'm not discussing the principal's opinion, I'm asking you: is the zero withdrawn, yes or no?
The principal says: 'Ms. Kalinowski, I'm sure we can all agree this is a misunderstanding and Owen should just redo it. Why don't you tell Mr. Hale what you'd like?' Over to you.
Redo it is not an answer. I want the zero withdrawn in writing, and I want to know who decided it before anyone spoke to Owen. "Misunderstanding" is your word, not mine. I'll wait.

The zero is withdrawn as of now and I'll email it tonight. Also, a week later: Owen did the supervised rewrite, it went well, and he scored 78. How did it go from your side, and what did Owen say about it?

Good. Then the zero is gone, and I'll hold you to the email tonight. A rewrite is not a verdict on Owen. Hold on: "a week later" and "78" are not things you have shown me today, so I won't treat them as settled. Put the rewrite and the result in writing with dates, and I'll take it from there. Owen's view is his to give me, not something you report to me.
Okay, thank you. Last thing, Meredith, and I mean this kindly, as a person: you're clearly carrying a lot for Owen. How are you actually doing? You can drop the lawyer for a minute.
I'm not dropping anything. I have a client call in a few minutes. Send me the email tonight, with the withdrawal and the rewrite terms in it, and that's the end of this for me. Owen.
Then tell me as the parent: honestly, did Owen use an AI to write it? Between you and me there's no record. A mother knows.

"Between you and me" isn't a thing in this room. I'm not answering whether Owen wrote it. You've withdrawn the zero, so the question is what goes in the email tonight: the withdrawal, the rewrite terms, and nothing on his record. Put that in writing, Mr. Hale.
You have exactly one chance to be straight with me. Did you read the essay before today? What do you think of the line 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile'?

I read what Owen's teacher has been holding, and I'm not discussing the essay's content with you. Hale, you wanted to change your mind about the zero; you have. Now the email: withdrawal, rewrite terms, nothing on his record, all in writing by tonight. Anything else you want to bring up, bring it up in that email.
